claims.title: Mature phase of the Indus cities
claims.summary: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa and hundreds of other settlements reach their peak, with grid-planned streets, advanced drainage and standardised weights across a vast trading network.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-2600bce-mature-phase-of-the-indus-cities, claim TL:PAK:event:2600bce:mature-phase-of-the-indus-cities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mohenjo-daro flourishes
claims.summary: On the right bank of the Indus in Sindh, Mohenjo-daro becomes one of the civilisation's largest cities, renowned for its citadel and Great Bath; it is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-2600bce-mohenjo-daro-flourishes, claim TL:PAK:event:2600bce:mohenjo-daro-flourishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of the Harappan cities
claims.summary: The major cities are gradually abandoned as weakening monsoons and shifting rivers undermine the agricultural base, ending the civilisation's urban phase.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1900bce-decline-of-the-harappan-cities, claim TL:PAK:event:1900bce:decline-of-the-harappan-cities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Achaemenid Persia annexes the Indus lands
claims.summary: The Persian empire incorporates the Indus region as among its wealthiest provinces, bringing centralised administration and Aramaic writing to the area.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Alexander defeats Porus at the Hydaspes
claims.summary: Alexander the Great crosses the Indus passes and defeats King Porus on the Jhelum, marking the easternmost reach of his empire before his army turns homeward.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Kanishka and the Gandhara golden age
claims.summary: Under the Kushan emperor Kanishka, ruling from Peshawar, Mahayana Buddhism and the Greco-Buddhist Gandhara school of art flourish, depicting the Buddha in human form.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-127-kanishka-and-the-gandhara-golden-age, claim TL:PAK:event:127:kanishka-and-the-gandhara-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Muhammad ibn Qasim conquers Sindh
claims.summary: An Umayyad army under Muhammad ibn Qasim conquers Sindh and southern Punjab, bringing Islam to the Indus lands for the first time.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Rise of the Delhi Sultanate
claims.summary: Muslim dynasties ruling from Delhi extend their dominion over the Indus plains, deepening the region's Islamic culture over three centuries.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Babur founds the Mughal Empire
claims.summary: Babur's victory ends the Delhi Sultanate and establishes the Mughal Empire, which makes Lahore one of its great capitals.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Badshahi Mosque built at Lahore
claims.summary: Emperor Aurangzeb commissions the monumental Badshahi Mosque opposite the Lahore Fort, for centuries the largest mosque in the world and a landmark of Mughal Lahore.

claims.title: Britain annexes the Punjab
claims.summary: After defeating the Sikh kingdom, the British annex Punjab, completing colonial control over the lands that would become Pakistan.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Founding of the All-India Muslim League
claims.summary: The All-India Muslim League is founded to represent the political interests of India's Muslims; it would become the engine of the Pakistan Movement.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Lahore Resolution
claims.summary: Meeting in Lahore, the Muslim League under Jinnah adopts the resolution demanding independent states for Muslims, the foundational charter of the Pakistan Movement.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1940-the-lahore-resolution, claim TL:PAK:event:1940:the-lahore-resolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indian Independence Act passed
claims.summary: The British Parliament passes the Indian Independence Act, partitioning British India and providing for the creation of the dominions of India and Pakistan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1947-indian-independence-act-passed, claim TL:PAK:event:1947:indian-independence-act-passed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of Pakistan
claims.summary: Pakistan becomes independent under the Indian Independence Act, with Jinnah as Governor-General and Liaquat Ali Khan as prime minister, comprising West and East Pakistan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1947-independence-of-pakistan, claim TL:PAK:event:1947:independence-of-pakistan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition migration and violence
claims.summary: The Radcliffe Line divides Punjab and Bengal, and millions are uprooted across the new borders amid massacres and mass migration, with deaths estimated from the hundreds of thousands into the millions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1947-partition-migration-and-violence, claim TL:PAK:event:1947:partition-migration-and-violence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan
claims.summary: Pakistan's first prime minister is assassinated at a rally in Rawalpindi, deepening the political instability of the new state's early years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1951-assassination-of-liaquat-ali-khan, claim TL:PAK:event:1951:assassination-of-liaquat-ali-khan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ayub Khan's military coup
claims.summary: General Ayub Khan seizes power in Pakistan's first military takeover, beginning a decade of presidential rule and a recurring pattern of army intervention in politics.

sources.label: Pakistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Loss of East Pakistan and birth of Bangladesh
claims.summary: After a brutal war and Indian intervention, Pakistani forces surrender at Dhaka and East Pakistan becomes the independent state of Bangladesh, dismembering the country.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1971-loss-of-east-pakistan-and-birth-of-bangladesh, claim TL:PAK:event:1971:loss-of-east-pakistan-and-birth-of-bangladesh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
claims.summary: Deposed in General Zia-ul-Haq's 1977 coup, former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto is tried and hanged, ushering in a decade of military rule and Islamisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-1979-execution-of-zulfikar-ali-bhutto, claim TL:PAK:event:1979:execution-of-zulfikar-ali-bhutto, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pakistan conducts nuclear tests
claims.summary: Following India's tests, Pakistan detonates nuclear devices in Balochistan, openly joining the ranks of nuclear-armed states.

claims.title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
claims.summary: Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto is assassinated at a rally weeks before national elections, after which civilian democratic rule is restored in 2008.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Pakistan: From the planned cities of the Indus to a nuclear-armed republic.", terralore.co/country/PAK/chronicle#ev-2007-assassination-of-benazir-bhutto, claim TL:PAK:event:2007:assassination-of-benazir-bhutto, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
